Classic L1 activity is falling and value capture is small
Seven signals with thresholds say when it is wrong

entries.caption: Is NEAR becoming the signing and settlement layer for other chains?

caption.text: The position: constructive on NEAR, as infrastructure that other chains use.

entries.caption: Signing: transactions touching v1.signer grew 6.4x in a year, to 29,515 a day, but are down 54% from the May peak.
Bridge and connector contracts are the cross-chain callers. Five callers make about 97% of sign calls.
Cross-chain share of sampled sign calls: 31.5% in August, 57.3% in October. Bridge calls stayed about flat; FastAuth calls fell.
Intents: about $134 million a day, up 79% in a year but only 8% above last November's high; down 12% on the month.
Value capture: Intents revenue to NEAR is about 12 times L1 fees, but only 0.51% of market cap a year, against 2.48% net supply growth.
Counter-evidence, with the same weight: daily active accounts are down 79% in a year.

caption.text: What would change my mind: seven signals, each with a threshold.
If signing and Intents volume both weaken, the thesis is wrong.

entries.caption: Real, early, thinly captured. Re-check on 2027-04-30.
